### Get it

Everything happens on your own device: no accounts, no tracking, no samples, nothing to license.

| Your computer | Download |
| --- | --- |
| Mac with Apple silicon (M1 and later) | `BleepBloop-mac-arm64.dmg` |
| Mac with an Intel chip | `BleepBloop-mac-x64.dmg` |
| Windows 10 or 11 | `BleepBloop-windows-x64-setup.exe` |
| Windows on Arm | `BleepBloop-windows-arm64-setup.exe` |
| Linux, any distro | `BleepBloop-linux-x86_64.AppImage` (Arm: `-arm64.AppImage`) |
| Debian or Ubuntu | `BleepBloop-linux-amd64.deb` (Arm: `-arm64.deb`) |
| A phone, or anything else | [bomkino.github.io/8bit-Voice](https://bomkino.github.io/8bit-Voice/), which you can add to your Home Screen |

These apps aren't signed by Apple or Microsoft, so each system asks once before it opens one. [Here's what to click.](https://github.com/bomkino/8bit-Voice#opening-it-the-first-time)

On a Mac, BleepBloop keeps itself up to date from here on: it checks once a day, and **BleepBloop › Check for Updates…** checks now. `appcast-arm64.xml` and `appcast-x64.xml` are its update feeds.

BleepBloop used to be called 8-bit Voice. The files named `8-bit-Voice-…` are the same apps under the old name, so links people already have keep working.

`SHA256SUMS.txt` has a checksum for every file.
